subject: Request: temporary model pin/lock for AtlasBank — expedited ask
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary model pin/lock for AtlasBank — expedited ask

Team,

Quick background: AtlasBank is moving rapidly toward procurement (expected signature target 2028-05-10). Their security and procurement teams have requested that, for auditability and deterministic output reasons, we provide a way to "pin" their tenant to a specific model artifact (redwood-gpt-xl-quantized-v2) for the first 90 days after go-live. They want this to be an explicit contractual guarantee so they can complete their external audit.

What they're asking from us:
- A temporary model pin (no automatic model swaps or transparent upgrades) for AtlasBank tenant in Hosted/Dedicated for an initial 90-day window.
- Confirmation of perf (latency p95) and cost delta vs default routing.
- A short operations playbook that explains how we will roll back or revert if regressions occur.

Why this matters now: procurement will not sign until the security team gets a product-level commitment. We have a verbal commitment but need an internal engineering/product decision and a one-page note for legal/finance.

Attachments: [Attachment: AtlasBank_Risk_Summary.pdf (pdf)], [Attachment: Draft_MAP_AtlasBank.xlsx (xlsx)]

Asks: can product/eng provide feasibility and a ballpark ETA + cost delta by EOD Monday (2028-05-06)? If we can't automate immediately, is a manual gating procedure acceptable as a short-term workaround?

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary model pin/lock for AtlasBank — expedited ask

Marissa / Grace —

Thanks for flagging. High level thoughts: pinning a tenant to a model variant is doable but has trade-offs. We can approach this in two ways:

Option A — Product-configured pin (short-term)
- Scope: we keep routing static for AtlasBank to redwood-gpt-xl-quantized-v2. No autoswap.
- Pros: fast (configuration change), minimal infra churn, low dev work.
- Cons: manual operations to change later; risk if model has a silent quality regression.

Option B — Platform-level model-lock feature (recommended for scale)
- Scope: add a routing flag + audit log + opt-out/rollforward APIs.
- Pros: auditable, safe rollouts, automated controls.
- Cons: requires engineering cycles (see David cc).

I need the following to give a tight estimate:
1) Do they require the pin for Hosted (shared infra) or Dedicated (reserved capacity)?
2) Are they okay with a documented manual change process for the first 30 days while we build a platform feature?

If they insist on a contractual guarantee without any manual caveat, engineering will need to scope production hardening. David, can you give a rough dev estimate for Option B?

— Irene
Product 
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 10:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary model pin/lock for AtlasBank — expedited ask

Irene / team —

Quick engineering readout after a quick spike:
- Feasibility: straightforward to implement a routing flag that pins tenant->model variant. Two parts: control-plane flag + routing enforcement in the runtime.
- Effort: estimate ~10 engineer-days (1 eng * 10d or 2 eng * 5d) for the MVP: control-plane change, route check, audit logging, basic QA. Add ~3-5 days for canary + SRE runbook.
- Perf/cost: quantized-v2 is ~18% cheaper per token than the non-quantized baseline in our benchmarks, but p95 latency is ~12% higher due to dequant path on current kernel stacks. If customer requires p95 <= existing SLO, we will need additional kernel tuning (~2-3 more eng-days, uncertain).
- Risk: pinned tenants won't benefit from silent model-quality fixes; we will need to implement an explicit "allowlist" for emergency swaps and a documented rollback process.

Short-term workaround: we can do Option A (manual pin) by setting a tenant config and documenting the manual change process. This would require an ops runbook and an engineer on-call during the first week of production.

Deliverables I can produce by Monday EOD (2028-05-07):
- A concise implementation estimate and a minimal runbook for manual pinning.
- A bullet list of QA checks and monitoring hooks required for contract sign-off.

Let me know if we should proceed with the manual short-term route while we scope the platform feature.

— David
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary model pin/lock for AtlasBank — expedited ask

Thanks David — this is great and actionable. A few clarifications from AtlasBank that change the ask slightly:
- They require the contractual guarantee but will accept a documented manual change process for the first 30 days as long as we commit to the platform feature roadmap and a firm timeline for automation.
- Procurement wants a one-page tech/ops note that summarizes the plan, cost delta, and fallbacks. Legal asked for explicit rollback triggers (e.g., model drift > X, security incident).
- Timeline: procurement expects the one-page note by 2028-05-08 so they can include it in the internal approval packet.

I'm attaching the procurement contact list. If you can produce the one-page doc + an implementation estimate by EOD Monday (2028-05-07), we should be able to keep the deal on the current timeline. We'll accept a small surcharge for the 90-day pin.

Attachments: [Attachment: Procurement_Contact_List.csv (csv)]

— Marissa
